newsitem.title: USA: Diverted campaign gifts not violation of muni rule.
newsitem.headline: Diverted campaign gifts not violation of muni rule.

text.p: Municipal bond firms whose campaign contributions to national Republican candidates were diverted to state and local campaigns are not in violation of regulations forbidding such contributions, the industry's chief regulator said Thursday.

"Those firms clearly indicated that their funds were to be used for other things," Christopher Taylor, executive director of the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board, said in an interview. "They were diverted from what their intended purposes were."

The New York Times reported this week that U.S. Sen Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, diverted a portion of campaign gifts intended for national Republican groups to state and local politicians in New York.

Goldman Sachs & Co, PaineWebber Group Inc, and Morgan Stanley Group Inc were among the donors listed. Under MSRB rules, those firms are restricted in their contributions to state and local politicians because the firms also handle municipal finance work.
But Taylor said as long as the firms were trying to contribute to national causes, the diversion is not their fault.

"Provided the firms have not done any tagging, have not done the wink and the nod that this stuff was to go to (N.Y. Gov.) Pataki's committee, they have no problem as far as I can see because this money did not go where they thought it was going to go," Taylor said.
The MSRB chief said he has spoken to the firms involved "in different forums" and they know the MSRB's position.

A PaineWebber spokesman said the firm's contribution "was intended for use by the Republican Senatorial Committee building fund and was clearly designated as such. This money was never intended to be made available to any state or local entity or person."
Officials at Goldman and Morgan Stanley were not immediately available for comment.
